key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in linear time, with a proven upper bound of 5(n−1) rounds, matching the known Ω(n) lower bound up to constants.
engineering_relevance: This gives a sharper worst-case guarantee for graph isomorphism refinement and related symmetry-detection pipelines, improving predictability for combinatorial and machine-learning graph methods.
method: Analyze stabilization rounds of the classical 2D Weisfeiler-Leman color refinement process.
Prove a new linear upper bound of 5(n−1), improving the prior O(n log n) bound.
Extend the argument to k-dimensional WL for k≥3, yielding an improved O(n^(k−1)/(k−2)! + n^(k−2)) bound.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical, derived from worst-case iteration analysis rather than experiments, and it improves the best known upper bound while asymptotically matching the lower bound.
watch_item: The guarantee concerns iteration count only; practical runtime still depends on implementation details and per-round cost, especially for larger k.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
